response.title: Lead routing system in n8n: intake, dedupe, enrichment, Slack alerts
response.description:
Please read the full brief before applying. It is long because we want fixed-price bids that are accurate.

1. About us

We are a B2B software company selling scheduling software to clinics. Our sales team has 12 reps in three regions (Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific), plus two senior reps who handle enterprise accounts. Marketing generates leads from several places, and today nobody owns the plumbing between those sources and the reps. Most of our customers are clinics with 5 to 50 staff, and a growing share are hospital groups, which is why enterprise routing matters to us.

2. The problem today

Leads arrive in four ways, and each one is handled differently:

- Demo requests from the website form land in a shared inbox.
- Pricing-page chat leads are exported from our chat tool once a day by our marketing coordinator.
- Webinar registrations come as a CSV after each webinar, usually 100 to 300 rows.
- Partner referrals arrive as emails from about 15 partner companies, each in a different format.

Our marketing coordinator copies all of this into a Google Sheet by hand, then posts in Slack asking who wants which lead, and reps claim leads in the thread. This takes her roughly 6 hours a week, and leads go cold: our median time from form submission to first contact is 19 hours. We also get duplicates when the same person registers for a webinar and later books a demo, and two reps sometimes contact the same person without knowing it.

Last quarter we estimate that around 30 leads were never contacted at all, because they sat in the shared inbox or arrived over a weekend. That is the number we most want to bring to zero.

3. What we want built

An n8n-based lead routing system that:

- takes in leads from all four sources automatically,
- cleans and validates them,
- merges duplicates instead of creating new records,
- enriches each lead with company size and industry,
- assigns each lead to the right rep using clear rules,
- notifies the rep in Slack and escalates if nobody acts,
- stores every lead in PostgreSQL as the source of truth, with a Google Sheet mirror for the sales manager,
- handles errors without losing a single lead, and
- is documented well enough that our in-house developer can maintain it after handover.

We already self-host n8n (Docker, latest stable version) and run PostgreSQL 15 on the same server. We use Google Workspace and Slack. We pay for an enrichment provider with a REST API that returns company size and industry from an email domain, and we will share its API docs with the freelancer we hire.

4. Requirements

4.1 Intake

- Website demo form: the form can post a webhook to n8n. Fields are first name, last name, work email, company, country, phone (optional) and message (optional).
- Pricing-page chat: the chat tool can send a webhook when a visitor leaves an email. Fields are email, name (sometimes missing), page URL and the chat transcript.
- Webinar registrations: we will drop each CSV into a shared Google Drive folder. The workflow should pick up new files in that folder, process every row and move the file to a "processed" subfolder when it is done.
- Partner referrals: partners send referrals to a dedicated inbox. Formats vary: some put the details in the email body, others attach a short form. Extract the name, email, company, country and the partner's name. If a referral can't be parsed, it must go to a review queue instead of being dropped.

4.2 Validation and normalization

- Lowercase and trim every email, and reject obviously invalid addresses.
- Free email domains such as gmail.com and outlook.com are allowed but flagged, since enrichment won't work for them.
- Normalize country names to ISO country codes.
- Normalize phone numbers when present.
- Every lead keeps its original source and the raw payload, so we can audit what came in.

4.3 Duplicate handling

- A lead is a duplicate if its email already exists in PostgreSQL.
- Duplicates are not dropped. They are merged into the existing lead, the new touchpoint is added to its history, and the assigned rep is told in Slack that their lead came back.
- If the existing lead is older than 180 days and was marked "closed lost", treat the new one as a fresh lead and route it again.

4.4 Enrichment

- Call our enrichment provider with the email domain.
- Store the company size band and the industry.
- If enrichment fails, or the domain belongs to a free email provider, continue without it. Routing must never wait on enrichment.
- The provider allows 10 requests per second, so please respect that limit, especially when a webinar CSV arrives.

4.5 Routing rules

- The region comes from the country code. We will give you the country-to-region table.
- Leads from companies with 500 or more employees go to the two senior reps, alternating between them.
- All other leads go round-robin to the reps in that region who are marked "available" in a small table we maintain.
- The round-robin must survive restarts, so store its pointer in PostgreSQL rather than in memory.
- If no rep in the region is available, assign the lead to that region's team lead.
- Working hours matter: a lead that arrives outside the assigned rep's working hours should still be assigned, but flagged as "next morning" in the Slack message.

4.6 Notifications

- Send the assigned rep a Slack direct message with the lead's name, company, country, source and a link to its row in the Google Sheet. Do not include the phone number or the chat transcript in Slack.
- Post a one-line summary in our #leads channel for every new lead.
- If the rep doesn't click "Claim" in the Slack message within 30 minutes during working hours, reassign the lead to the next rep in the rotation and notify the team lead.
- Send a daily digest at 9:00 local time to the sales manager, with new leads by source and region, unclaimed leads and any errors.

4.7 Storage

- PostgreSQL is the source of truth. Please propose the schema; we expect at least a leads table, a touchpoints table and an assignments table.
- The Google Sheet is a read-only mirror for the sales manager and should be updated within 5 minutes of any change.
- Keep the raw payload of every intake event for 90 days, then delete it automatically.

4.8 Error handling and retries

- Retry with exponential backoff for Slack, the enrichment API and Google Sheets.
- Failed events go to a dead-letter table with the error message, so nothing is ever lost.
- Give us a simple way to replay dead-letter events once the cause is fixed.
- The daily digest must list every error from the last 24 hours.

4.9 Logging and monitoring

- Log every lead's path: received, validated, merged or created, enriched, assigned, notified and claimed.
- We want to answer "what happened to this lead?" in under a minute by looking at one table.
- Keep these logs for at least 12 months.

4.10 Security

- Keep all credentials in n8n's credential store, with nothing hardcoded in Code nodes.
- Use a PostgreSQL user with only the permissions this system needs.
- Send no personal data to Slack beyond what is listed in 4.6.

4.11 Configuration

- Rep availability, working hours, territories and the enterprise threshold (500 employees) must live in PostgreSQL tables or n8n variables, not inside workflow logic, so our sales manager can change them without editing a workflow.
- Changes to these settings should take effect on the next lead, without restarting n8n.
- Please document every setting in the README, with its default value and what it controls.

4.12 Testing and staging

- Build and test everything against the staging database first.
- Provide a test mode that sends every Slack message to a test channel instead of to reps.
- Include a small set of test leads we can rerun after any change, covering every source and every routing rule.
- We move to production only after we sign off on staging.

4.13 Performance

- A webinar CSV of 300 rows should be fully processed, enriched and assigned within 15 minutes.
- A single form or chat lead should reach the assigned rep within 2 minutes of submission.

5. Volumes

We get about 400 leads a month today, with peaks of 60 in a single day after webinars. We expect volume to double within a year, so please don't design anything that only works at today's volume.

6. Deliverables

- The n8n workflows, exported and committed to our Git repository.
- SQL migration files for the schema.
- A README covering setup, the routing rules, how to change a rep's availability, how to replay failed events and how to add a new lead source.
- A short architecture diagram showing every workflow, table and external service.
- A 30-minute handover call, recorded, with our developer and our sales manager.

7. Milestones

- Milestone 1 ($1,200): intake from all four sources, validation, duplicate handling and PostgreSQL storage, with the Google Sheet mirror.
- Milestone 2 ($1,400): enrichment, routing rules, Slack notifications, claiming and reassignment.
- Milestone 3 ($900): error handling, dead-letter replay, the daily digest, logging, documentation and handover.

8. Acceptance criteria

- We will send 50 test leads across all four sources, including duplicates, free-email leads, a malformed partner email and a lead from a country with no available rep. Each one must end up in the right place, assigned to the right rep, with a complete log.
- No lead may be lost when Slack or the enrichment API is down for 15 minutes.
- Our developer must be able to add a fifth lead source by following the README alone.
- Our sales manager must be able to change any setting in 4.11 without help, which we will test during the handover call.

9. What we provide

- Admin access to our n8n instance and a staging PostgreSQL database.
- A Slack workspace for testing.
- Sample files for every lead source.
- The country-to-region table and the rep availability table.
- One hour a week with our sales manager for questions.

10. Out of scope

- Changes to our website form or chat tool beyond configuring their webhooks.
- Dashboards beyond the daily digest.
- Any CRM migration. We are not moving to a CRM this year.

11. How we'll work together

- A kickoff call in the first week to confirm the schema and the routing rules.
- A short written update every Friday: what was done, what's next and anything blocked.
- Questions go in the project chat, and we reply within one working day.
- Our developer reviews the work at the end of each milestone before we release payment.

12. Questions for applicants

Please answer these three questions in your proposal:

1. How would you keep the round-robin fair and correct when two leads arrive in the same second?
2. How would you parse partner referral emails that don't follow a fixed format, and what would go to the review queue?
3. Which part of this project do you see as the biggest risk, and how would you reduce it in the first milestone?

We will shortlist proposals that answer all three questions clearly. Generic proposals will not be considered.
